field.label: Enable Tracking
field.comment: Kill switch — disables the frontend beacon and the ingest endpoint's writes entirely.

field.label: Primary Attribution Model
field.comment: Which ad click gets credit for a sale, when a customer clicked more than one ad before buying. Last Touch (the default, and the industry standard) credits the ad that brought the customer back for their final visit before checkout. First Touch instead credits the very first ad that ever brought them to the store.

field.label: Report Aggregation Lookback (days)
field.comment: How many recent days the nightly rollup recomputes. Events arrive through a queue, so a visit at 23:59 can be consumed after the 02:00 run — re-sweeping recent days picks those up. The rollup REPLACES each day it recomputes rather than adding to it, so a wider window costs time but can never double-count.

field.label: Beacon Console Logging
field.comment:
Makes the storefront beacon narrate every decision to the browser console: which event type it chose and why, consent and cookie state, each checkout step it detects, and whether each request was sent, deduplicated or suppressed. Leave this off in production — it is a diagnostic, not a feature.
You can also switch it on for one browsing session, without touching this setting, by adding ?adsanalytics_debug=1 to any storefront URL. That survives navigation, so it stays on through a whole landing → cart → checkout walkthrough. Turn it back off with ?adsanalytics_debug=0.

field.label: Sampling Rate (%)
field.comment: Optional load-shedding lever for high-traffic stores. Default 100.

group.label: Traffic Classification (Platforms & Search Engines)
group.comment:
These three lists control how a visit is classified as paid, organic, referral or direct traffic. To support a new ad platform (Pinterest, say) or a new regional search engine, just add a row below — nothing else needs to change.

Sensible defaults are already filled in, so the store works correctly out of the box; you only need to edit these if you use a platform or search engine that is not already listed.

field.label: Paid Platform / Click-ID Map
field.comment:
Click ID Parameter is the signal that classifies a visit as paid, and it comes from the URL a shopper actually arrives on — any value not listed here is rejected, so this list also acts as a safety check.
Default Source is what source becomes for this platform (meta → facebook).
Alt Sources are utm_source values that override Default Source when present — meta ships instagram, which is how an Instagram click is told apart from a Facebook one without naming either in code. platform_code itself never changes: it stays meta in both cases.

field.label: Paid Mediums (no click ID)
field.comment: For manually-tagged paid links that carry no click ID, e.g. ?utm_medium=cpc. Matched case-insensitively, so listing cpc also covers CPC.

field.label: Organic Search-Engine Domains
field.comment: Registrable domains only — google.com, never .google.com or google.*. Matched at a label boundary, so notgoogle.com does not match but mail.google.com does. Wildcards are unsupported by design: list each TLD as its own row mapping to the same engine name (yandex.com and yandex.ru → yandex).

field.label: How to provide spend data
field.comment:
The ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) report needs to know how much you spent on ads for each platform. There is no field to type that in here — instead, you place a file on the server, and the report reads it from there.

Where to put the file: inside your Magento installation, at var/aavirbhava/adsanalytics/adspend/<platform>.csv — for example var/aavirbhava/adsanalytics/adspend/google.csv for Google, or .../meta.csv for Meta (Facebook/Instagram). Ask whoever manages your server/hosting to place it there if you do not have direct file access yourself. Currently only Google and Meta are supported this way; other platforms, or a platform with no file yet, simply show "no data" in the ROAS report rather than a zero.

What the file should contain: a first row with the column names, then one row per day per campaign, like this:
date,campaign,spend
2026-09-19,spring_sale,42.50
2026-09-19,brand_awareness,18.00

date is YYYY-MM-DD, campaign should match the campaign name you already use in your ad tracking links, and spend is a plain number in your store's currency (no currency symbol). A row with a mistake in it is skipped rather than breaking the whole file.

This is a manual, once-in-a-while file update, not a live feed — nothing updates it automatically. If you want your ad spend to update on its own from Google Ads or Meta Ads, ask your developer; that can be added without changing how this report itself works.

group.label: Ingest Rate Limiting
group.comment:
Limits how many tracking events a single visitor can send in a short time, to stop a bot or a scripted attack from flooding your store's tracking data. The limit is applied per visitor together with their network address, so it cannot be avoided by simply generating new visitor IDs.

Going over the limit never shows an error to the shopper — it just quietly stops recording further events for that visitor until the window below resets. A tracking feature must never slow down or interrupt browsing or checkout.

field.label: Max Requests Per Window
field.comment: Best-effort fixed window, not an exact quota — a concurrent burst can overshoot slightly. This is load shedding, not access control.

field.label: Logging Level
field.comment: Rejected + Externally Referred (the default) logs failed/invalid requests plus visits that arrived from an ad, a search engine or another website — these are the ones most likely to reveal a tracking parameter this store does not yet recognise. Visits where the shopper typed the address directly, or used a bookmark, are not logged, since there is nothing external to learn from. Switch to All Requests only temporarily, if you need to debug the full visitor journey — note that this stores the complete raw data for every single request.

field.label: Request Log Retention (days)
field.comment: Kept shorter than the retention period below, since this log stores raw incoming request data rather than a summarised report.

field.label: Raw Visit/Funnel Event Retention (days)
field.comment: Your daily summary reports (the dashboard and grid) are kept forever no matter what you set here — this only controls how long the detailed, per-visitor data is kept.
